questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a future time.
questions.question: By the time you arrive, I ___ dinner.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in the past, continues now.
questions.question: She ___ in London for five years now.

questions.def: Stative verbs like 'know' don't use continuous tenses.
questions.question: He is knowing the answer, but he won't say.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: emphasizes duration of activity.
questions.question: I ___ for my exam all morning.

questions.def: Present simple: scheduled future events.
questions.question: The train ___ at 6:00 PM tomorrow.

questions.def: Present perfect: action not completed at the time of speaking.
questions.question: They ___ their house yet.

questions.def: Stative verbs like 'own' don't use continuous tenses.
questions.question: She is owning a beautiful car now.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started and continues.
questions.question: He ___ on the project since last week.

questions.def: Present continuous: future arrangement.
questions.question: I ___ a new car next month.

questions.def: Present continuous: changing situation.
questions.question: The price of gas ___ constantly.

questions.def: Present continuous with 'always' expresses annoying habits.
questions.question: He is always borrowing my pens; it really annoys me!

questions.def: Stative verb 'believe' usually in simple present.
questions.question: I ___ you.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started and continues.
questions.question: She ___ about it all day.

questions.def: Past continuous is needed; present tenses incorrect.
questions.question: He ___ TV when I called.

questions.def: 'Living' needs 'been' after 'has' for present perfect continuous.
questions.question: She has living here since 2000.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: duration from past to present.
questions.question: How long ___ you ___ here?

questions.def: Present perfect: experience at an unspecified time before now.
questions.question: I ___ that movie three times already.

questions.def: Simple present: habitual action.
questions.question: He ___ to the gym every day.

questions.def: Stative verbs like 'know' don't use continuous form.
questions.question: She is knowing the answer now, apparently.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: duration of an action.
questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour!

questions.def: Present Perfect: Action that started in past and relevant now.
questions.question: He ___ the guitar since he was a child.

questions.def: Present continuous: future arrangement.
questions.question: They ___ a meeting at 3 pm tomorrow.

questions.def: Habitual actions use Simple Present, not Present Continuous.
questions.question: She is having a headache every day this week.

questions.def: Stative verbs like 'own' usually in simple present.
questions.question: She ___ a cat.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action over a period.
questions.question: I ___ tired lately.

questions.def: Present continuous: action happening at the moment.
questions.question: She ___ in Paris right now.

questions.def: 'Is always forgetting' expresses annoyance, not 'to forget'.
questions.question: He is always to forget his keys.

questions.def: Past simple: completed action in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him yesterday.

questions.def: Present simple: fact or general truth.
questions.question: The sun ___ in the east.

questions.def: Present perfect: action that started in the past and continues.
questions.question: I ___ him since last year.
